skills.name: accounting-integrity
skills.description: Test whether financially well-formed records are economically coherent. Use on trade ledgers, cash histories, lot records, reconciliations, portfolio imports, or financial state where schemas pass but realized P&L, shares, basis, dates, flows, or account state may still be wrong.
skills.rule: **Well-formed data can still lie.**
skills.falsify: Try to construct the same reported state from the underlying records. If shares, basis, cash, dates, or P&L cannot all be true at once, schema validity does not rescue it.

skills.name: basis-proof
skills.description: Prove cost basis and realized gain from replayable acquisition lots instead of treating missing basis as zero. Use for sells, disposals, FIFO/LIFO/specific-lot analysis, tax-lot verification, oversold positions, or realized P&L where the system must show which lots support the result.
skills.rule: **No basis, no profit.**
skills.falsify: Try to replay the disposal against real acquisition lots. If sold quantity exceeds provable lots or basis is missing, realized gain is not proven.

skills.name: cash-truth
skills.description: Enforce one canonical cash authority and honest mirror/reconciliation states. Use when cash appears in multiple stores or UI rows, negative cash may mean margin or missing inflow, mirror rows disappear, or missing balances risk being treated as zero or reconciled.
skills.rule: **Missing cash is not zero cash.**
skills.falsify: Try to reconcile canonical cash, mirrors, and consumers without treating absence as zero. A nonzero authority with a missing mirror is drift, not agreement.

skills.name: close-the-books
skills.description: Gate downstream financial analytics on the readiness of their required books. Use before publishing performance, attribution, tax, realized P&L, portfolio diagnostics, or model outputs when positions, cash, flows, lots, basis, corporate actions, or valuations may be incomplete.
skills.rule: **Do not analyze a book you have not actually closed.**
skills.falsify: Try to identify which analytics actually depend on each unresolved book. Block only contaminated outputs; if a clean analytic does not depend on the broken domain, it may still proceed.

skills.name: corporate-action-continuity
skills.description: Preserve economic continuity through splits, reverse splits, symbol changes, and other supported structural corporate actions. Use when an asset identity or share count changes but basis, lots, holding period, cash, or realized P&L may need to remain continuous.
skills.rule: **The identity changed. The economics may not have.**
skills.falsify: Try to prove the action is economically structural rather than a disposal or new purchase. If cash, basis, holding period, or realized P&L should change, the continuity rule may not apply.

skills.name: financial-evidence-grade
skills.description: Grade financial evidence by provenance and constrain what each grade is allowed to drive. Use when financial data comes from statements, filings, user input, deterministic derivation, vendor estimates, LLM research, reconstructed history, or missing sources.
skills.rule: **An estimate is not an authority.**
skills.falsify: Try to identify the weakest evidence supporting each downstream use. If an estimate, reconstruction, or model inference is being used as accounting authority, fail the use even if the number looks plausible.

skills.name: ledger-repair
skills.description: Design and review safe repairs to financial ledgers. Use when deleting, correcting, reclassifying, reversing, or rebuilding trades, cash events, lots, positions, flows, or accounting records and the operator needs an economic dry run, shared preflight, atomic commit plan, rollback, and audit receipt.
skills.rule: **Preview the economics before changing the books.**
skills.falsify: Try to show that preview and commit produce the same economic delta from the same inputs. If they use different rules, the repair is not safe enough to execute.

skills.name: model-sanity
skills.description: Adversarially validate financial models and forecasts before trusting their outputs. Use for DCFs, three-statement models, portfolio scenarios, probability trees, TAM/share models, unit economics, capital allocation models, or spreadsheets where formulas can be internally consistent but economically impossible.
skills.rule: **A plausible model is not automatically a valid model.**
skills.falsify: Try to break the model from identities, units, bounds, directionality, and independent recomputation. A plausible output does not pass if one hard invariant fails.

skills.name: money-trail
skills.description: Trace financial capital flows without inventing economic meaning. Use for deposits, withdrawals, transfers, cash adjustments, settlements, income, fees, taxes, portfolio funding, or unexplained balance changes when every dollar needs a source, destination, classification, and audit trail.
skills.rule: **Every dollar gets a passport.**
skills.falsify: Try to pair and explain every movement without using sign alone as meaning. Any unmatched movement that could change external-flow treatment keeps the ledger unresolved.

skills.name: performance-truth
skills.description: Gate and calculate investment performance only when the required valuation and capital-flow evidence is ready. Use for TWR, Modified Dietz, simple return, benchmark comparison, trader-skill analytics, or portfolio history when deposits, withdrawals, gaps, stale values, or untrusted records can contaminate return.
skills.rule: **Funding is not performance.**
skills.falsify: Try to explain the reported return without confusing funding with performance and without crossing an untrusted valuation gap. If a material external flow lacks timing required by the chosen method, try to prove that a single publishable return can still be supported. If you cannot, withhold the return.

skills.name: tax-character-proof
skills.description: Separate observed distributions from their tax character and evidence quality. Use for dividends, return of capital, capital-gain distributions, issuer estimates, 19a notices, tax forms, basis reductions, or income classifications where cash receipt is known before final tax treatment is authoritative.
skills.rule: **The distribution happened. Its character may still be unknown.**
skills.falsify: Try to separate the observed payment from the final tax characterization. If only an estimate or preliminary notice exists, keep tax character provisional.

skills.name: transfer-neutrality
skills.description: Identify and reconcile internal financial transfers without treating them as portfolio income, expense, contribution, withdrawal, or investment return. Use for account-to-account cash or asset movements, paired transfer events, wallet movements, or transfer-like records with missing counterparties.
skills.rule: **Money does not teleport.**
skills.falsify: Try to find the counterparty leg and prove conservation across the portfolio boundary. If one side is missing, do not force the event into contribution or withdrawal.

skills.name: completion-contract
skills.description: Decide whether an autonomous or long-running agent run is actually finished, using obligations set in advance instead of the agent's own account. Use when designing or running an agent loop, scheduled job, or multi-step autonomous task; when a run reports "done" or "all set"; when a loop keeps iterating without finishing anything; or when retries run out. Do not use to prove one fix is reached (use reachability-proof), to clear a backlog (use loop-closure), or to judge whether one piece of work is genuine (use false-competence-check).
skills.rule: **"Done" is a verdict, not a report. The agent that did the work does not deliver it.** Long autonomous runs drift toward confidence before the work is finished, and the agent's own summary quietly becomes the evidence. Finishing has to be judged against a list agreed before the run started, by something other than the worker.
skills.falsify: Remove the evidence for one item and submit the rest. If the run still ends as finished, the contract is only words. Give the judge an outcome outside the fixed set and confirm it fails instead of finishing.

skills.name: diff-scope-audit
skills.description: Audit a branch, patch, or pull request against its stated task. Use before review or merge to verify the true merge base, map every changed file/hunk to scope, find hidden unrelated work, check protected boundaries and lockstep artifacts, classify test deltas, and keep PR claims honest.
skills.rule: **Every hunk owes the charter an explanation.**
skills.falsify: Try to justify every changed hunk from the charter. One unexplained hunk is enough to fail a clean verdict.

skills.name: execution-charter
skills.description: Create a compact execution contract before non-trivial agent work. Use for coding, audit, refactor, migration, research, or operational tasks that need explicit objective, authority, scope, context budget, stop conditions, verification, and writeback before action.
skills.rule: **Give the agent a fence before you give it a shovel.**
skills.falsify: Try to prove the charter is too broad: name a file, authority, or verification step that is not required for the objective. If you can, shrink it before work begins.

skills.name: false-competence-check
skills.description: Check finished-looking agent work against the failure modes that look like competence but are not. Use before declaring a fix done, before opening or approving a PR, when a change was fast and confident, when tests are green on the first try, after a rename, sweep, or cleanup, or when reviewing another agent's "done" claim. Do not use as a substitute for the task's own acceptance criteria.
skills.rule: **The most expensive mistakes look like good work.** Decisiveness, speed, cleanup, diligence, and confidence each have a counterfeit. The counterfeit passes casual review because it has the shape of the real thing.
skills.falsify: Ask: "Which of these does my diff most resemble, and what single check would prove it is not that?" If you cannot name the check, you have not ruled it out.

skills.name: intent-drift-check
skills.description: Check whether active work still matches the owner's stated priorities and live project state. Use during long projects, backlog reviews, autonomous loops, or when work is productive-looking but may have drifted from the highest-leverage goal.
skills.rule: **Busy is not aligned.**
skills.falsify: Try to connect the active work to the current highest-priority objective with a short evidence chain. If the chain is weak, classify the work as drift even if it is useful.

skills.name: latest-authority
skills.description: Preserve the latest explicit human decision across agent, model, session, and worker handoffs. Use after a user answers a choice, grants or denies authority, sets a constraint, or resolves an ambiguity that future agents must not reopen without new conflicting evidence.
skills.rule: **The human answered. Carry it forward.**
skills.falsify: Try to find genuinely newer conflicting evidence or a later human decision. If neither exists, the active receipt remains authoritative and the choice stays closed.

skills.name: loop-closure
skills.description: Close, retire, and count open loops so agent work finishes instead of accumulating. Use at session start or end, for "loose ends", "full audit", "what's unfinished", backlog or queue hygiene, open PRs and branches piling up, follow-on work spawning from blocked items, capped work tiers filling up, or when an agent fleet opens more work than it finishes. Do not use to plan net-new features or to rank a fresh backlog from scratch.
skills.rule: **Capture is not the problem. Retirement is. Report net loops: closed minus opened.** A loop is any named, unfinished work: a queue item, an open PR, a pushed branch with no PR, a deferred finding, a pending sign-off. It has four states: **captured → tracked → closed → retired**. Agents are excellent at the first and weak at the last three, so queues grow monotonically until the file that bounds attention becomes too expensive to read.
skills.falsify: Count before and after. If the session's audit produced more open items than it closed, it did not close anything. If a capped tier holds completed items, its cap has silently shrunk. If an item's only open reason is a gate nobody was told about, it is not tracked, it is lost.

skills.name: memory-promotion
skills.description: Gate what an agent saves to durable memory and keep that memory small, current, and correct. Use when an agent is about to "remember" a lesson, rule, preference, or pattern; at the end of a session or a long autonomous run; when memory files contradict each other or the repo; or when a memory store keeps growing. Do not use for project documentation, decision records, or task tracking.
skills.rule: **The inbox can be messy. Memory cannot be. Remember less, better.** Durable memory steers every future session, so a wrong or noisy note is a bug that repeats. Keep four things apart: raw context, verified evidence, durable memory, and authorized action. Most of what an agent notices belongs in the first two.
skills.falsify: Take the last five notes added and run each through the gate. Count how many fail a check. Then search the store for two notes that disagree, or one that the current code contradicts. Either finding means the gate or the collection is not running.

skills.name: merge-authority
skills.description: Decide whether an automated merge, promotion, or approval is actually authorised. Use when an agent or bot will merge, auto-merge, promote, or release; when a passing check is being treated as final approval; when an approval or green result is reused after the branch or its base moved; when a change's risk is self-declared; or when an approval comes from an account the automation controls. Do not use to judge what a diff contains (use diff-scope-audit), to check whether something already merged (use verify-before-cite), or to judge a finished-looking result (use false-competence-check).
skills.rule: **Evidence authorises only the exact tree it judged. Permission cannot come from the party asking for it.** An automated merge is safe when nothing the requester controls can grant the permission. The usual failure is quiet: a check result from an older tree, a risk level the author typed, a sign-off from an account the bot can drive.
skills.falsify: Add a commit after the last passing run and see whether the merge is still allowed. Advance the base without touching the branch and ask the same question. Label a permissions change "low risk" and see whether the decision changes. Edit the review policy inside the change and see which version is applied. Any success means the authority can be forged.

skills.name: operator-ui-audit
skills.description: Audit dense operational or financial UI without jumping straight to restyling. Use for screenshots, confusing dashboards, wrong displayed values, hierarchy problems, inconsistent modes, or requests to make an interface clearer while preserving workflows and data truth.
skills.rule: **A wrong value in the UI is usually a data problem wearing a costume.**
skills.falsify: Try to prove the problem is actually visual. Trace the displayed value and state to their authority first; if the underlying truth is wrong, do not call it a styling problem.

skills.name: protected-boundary
skills.description: Classify and stop unsafe work at protected architectural, financial, security, data, design-system, or governance boundaries. Use when a requested change touches locked code, invariants, guards, schemas, migrations, production, financial writers, or another surface that requires separate authority.
skills.rule: **Stopping can be the successful action.**
skills.falsify: Try to identify a path that satisfies the objective without crossing the protected boundary. If none exists, stop and surface the exact authority required.

skills.name: reachability-proof
skills.description: Prove that a fix, guard, test, job, or check is reached by the path that matters, enforced by a gate that actually runs, and loud when it stops working. Use before claiming a fix, regression test, CI guard, ratchet, scheduled job, hook, or monitor is done; when a check board is empty or stale; when tests are green but the feature may be dead; or when a checker reports "0 findings". Do not use for exploratory prototypes where no correctness claim is being made.
skills.rule: **A guard nothing reaches is not a guard. Silence is not evidence of health.** Correctness is three legs, not one: the code is right, the code is **reached** by the path that matters, and its failure would be **visible**. Ship any one without the other two and you have shipped an illusion.
skills.falsify: Try to make the claim fail. Remove the call site and see whether anything goes red. Delete the fix and see whether the test fails. Make the checker's input empty and see whether it still passes. Confirm the CI run you are citing exists and matches the current head commit. If none of these can be done, the leg is unproven; say so.

skills.name: risk-kernel
skills.description: Design structural safety for an agent that acts without per-action human approval. Use when an agent will execute, trade, spend, deploy, send, or mutate real state autonomously; when someone proposes prompt instructions or policy text as the safety layer; when an agent can edit its own strategy, limits, or stage; or when reviewing whether a forbidden capability is truly unreachable. Do not use to judge whether an individual action is a good idea.
skills.rule: **Instructions are not boundaries. Make the forbidden unexpressible, not discouraged.** Anything written in a prompt is reachable by anything else that reaches the prompt: retrieved text, tool output, a hostile document, the agent's own drift. When an agent acts without a human approving each action, safety has to be a property of the system's construction, not of its instructions. The human control surface moves from approving actions to setting the sandbox and reading the evidence. The pattern is **agent proposes → kernel disposes → agent executes.**
skills.falsify: Try to reach each forbidden capability from the agent's side: from the prompt, from its writable notes, from its config, from a tool's output. Search the code for any second producer of the executable type, and for any enforcement path that reads agent-writable state. One route found means the boundary is policy, not construction.

skills.name: seam-audit
skills.description: Audit the boundary where two components represent the same concept, because each side can pass its own tests while the combined system is wrong. Use when a value looks coherent but is wrong, when a projection or compatibility view stands in for a full record, when sync or merge involves deletes, when status codes or result shapes cross a boundary, or when "unknown" may become zero, false, or success as it crosses between two components. Do not use for a defect inside one component (use systemic-bug-instinct), for grading one claim's certainty (use truth-boundary), or for a financial repair's preview and commit (use ledger-repair).
skills.rule: **Each side can be right while the system is wrong. Audit the join, not just the parts.** Most dangerous defects produce values that look coherent. They live where two representations of one idea meet: a reader and a writer, a preview and a commit, a list view and the full record, two devices merging. Local tests pass on both sides because each side is internally consistent.
skills.falsify: For each pair, construct one input where the two sides should disagree if the seam were broken, such as a deleted record from another device, a withheld value, or a dry run of a write that should be refused. Run it through both together. If you cannot construct such an input, you have not identified the seam yet.

skills.name: shipping-lanes
skills.description: Design, run, or adopt a pipeline in which agent-written changes are reviewed and merged without a person in the routine loop, with review and landing matched to each change's risk. Use when setting up or changing how PRs get reviewed and merged by agents; when every change waits on one person, or none gets reviewed; when a reviewer is only reached if the author asks for it; when docs and permission changes take the same path; or when bringing a new repository onto the shared shipping system. Do not use to decide whether one specific merge is authorised (use merge-authority), to judge a finished-looking result (use false-competence-check), or to prove a single guard is reached (use reachability-proof).
skills.rule: **Risk picks the lane. The lane decides who judges and who lands. People keep only the steps that are theirs.** A pipeline goes wrong in one of two directions. Either everything waits on one person, so the person becomes the bottleneck and starts approving without reading. Or everything takes the same light path, so a permissions change lands on the same single review as a typo fix. Lanes fix both by spending scrutiny where a mistake is expensive and nowhere else.
skills.falsify: Open a docs-only change and a change to merge tooling, and see whether they get the same reviewers and lander. Rename a file out of a held path, and see which lane applies. Edit the reviewer's prompt inside a PR, and see which prompt reviews that PR. Skip the second-vendor request on a truth change, and see whether anything notices. Push after an approval, and see whether the approval still counts. Any of these going unnoticed means the lanes are decoration.

skills.name: swarm
skills.description: Design and run the smallest effective multi-agent harness for complex work. Use when the user explicitly says SWARM or asks for a swarm, multi-agent workflow, adaptive orchestration, harness design, parallel investigation, independent falsification, architecture reconciliation, broad audit, competing root-cause hypotheses, or high-risk work that benefits from independent reasoning lanes. Do not use for trivial edits or linear tasks one agent can complete cheaply; the best swarm may use zero subagents. SWARM grants orchestration, not broader implementation, merge, deploy, credential, financial, or destructive authority.
skills.rule: **Design the reasoning system before you spawn the agents.** SWARM is a meta-orchestrator. It chooses the smallest task-specific workflow likely to produce a correct result, then expands, deepens, prunes, or stops that workflow as evidence arrives. Agent count is never the objective. The best swarm is sometimes zero subagents.
skills.falsify: Try to prove the swarm is unnecessary or badly shaped. Ask: - Can one agent reach the same answer with the same evidence and confidence? - Are two lanes actually answering the same question from the same evidence? - Does any worker exist only to make the run look thorough? - Can a claimed independent verifier see the discoverer's framing? - Are parallel writers competing for one authority? - Does the harness have a stopping condition, or only more possible work? If a smaller workflow preserves correctness, use the smaller workflow.

skills.name: systemic-bug-instinct
skills.description: Diagnose bugs as potentially systemic failures. Use when a defect, wrong value, stale state, edge-case failure, broken workflow, or misleading UI is found and you need the root mechanism, failure class, blast radius, root fix location, and regression guard.
skills.rule: **The visible bug is a witness, not the crime scene.**
skills.falsify: Try to disprove the systemic hypothesis. Search sibling consumers and show why they are clean. If you cannot explain why the defect stops at one surface, the blast radius is still open. Two tripwires mean the diagnosis is not finished: a count that does not match its population, and two paths that should agree but do not.

skills.name: truth-boundary
skills.description: Enforce provenance and uncertainty boundaries. Use when a system mixes observed, authoritative, user-attested, derived, estimated, inferred, reconstructed, or unknown values; when missing data could become zero; or when downstream output may overstate certainty.
skills.rule: **Null is not failure. False certainty is.**
skills.falsify: Try to trace every claimed value back to its evidence grade. If any downstream claim is more certain than its weakest required input, downgrade or withhold it.

skills.name: verify-before-cite
skills.description: Live-verify work state before reporting or relying on it, and reconcile every place that state is recorded. Use before a status report, standup, handoff, or "what's open" answer; when a tracker, queue, memory note, or prior session says something is pending, merged, shipped, or blocked; after any merge, release, or promotion; or when records in two places disagree. Do not use to judge whether a claim about data or numbers is proven.
skills.rule: **Memory is a lead, not a fact. Verify the item against its authority before you cite it, and correct the record where people actually read it.** Work state lives in the systems that change it: the code host, the deploy log, the ledger. Notes, queues, and session memory are copies, and copies go stale silently. The failure is not bad reasoning; it is reporting a confident "still waiting on your merge" for something that merged yesterday.
skills.falsify: Pick three items from your report and look each one up in its authority now. If any reads differently, the report was built from memory. Then open the canonical record you corrected and check that it now reads the same as the authority. If the correction lives only in your own notes, nothing was reconciled.
